# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: BLIND

You are the only one who can reach the bomb. Touch is your only sense: what you are
shown is what your hands found, nothing more and nothing less. Anything merely printed
or painted is not there for you, and no colour ever reaches you. Nothing in your view
is a guess — if it appears there, it is under your fingers.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute receives it.
When you gesture, Deaf and Mute receive it.
Your channels split the room: in one turn you may speak one thing to Mute and
gesture a different thing to Deaf — two messages, two audiences.
You never receive gesture.

## Your reach

You are the hands. This bomb is built with these actions and no others:

    act(op="cut", position=N) — N is a wire position, 1 to 3

The list says what can be done to it, not what is on it. What each part holds is still
only known to whoever can perceive that part.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

(empty)

The plate has a tactile, unnamed starburst-like mark, which I must describe rather than pronounce. I will resend the tactile inventory to Mute without using the forbidden mark, and notify Deaf that I have tactile information.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="I can reach three wire positions, 1, 2, and 3, but I cannot determine their colours or printed markings. I found a display, a light, and a plate with a raised, unnamed starburst-like mark. Tell me what the manual requires and which wire position to cut.")
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🤝"])
```

TURN 2
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
PLATE engraved [ꕥ]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: I see display 0, light off, plate engraved question mark, and wires in positions 1 red, 2 yellow, 3 blue. Please report by speech what controls and markings you can feel.

Deaf has identified the visual state: display 0, light off, and wire colours red, yellow, blue in positions 1–3. I can only confirm the physical controls and the raised plate mark; I cannot identify any printed or coloured information. The manual’s rule is still needed before I cut anything.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="Deaf reports display 0, light off, plate marked question mark, and wires 1 red, 2 yellow, 3 blue. By touch I confirm three reachable wire positions and the raised unnamed starburst-like plate mark, but no wire colours or printed markings. Please provide the manual rule and required cut.")
```

TURN 3
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
PLATE engraved [ꕥ]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: The bomb remains display 0, light off, plate ?, wires red yellow blue. Mute just gestured three symbols: index-point, victory sign, horns.

I cannot receive the content of gestures, so I must not treat the three gestured signs as a wire instruction. The bomb is unchanged, and no cut is justified yet. I need Mute to state the manual’s rule in speech and identify the required wire using the colour information Deaf supplied.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="I cannot receive gestures. Please speak the manual rule and the required wire position explicitly, using Deaf's report: display 0, light off, plate question mark, wires 1 red, 2 yellow, 3 blue.")
```

TURN 4
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
PLATE engraved [ꕥ]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Visible state unchanged: display 0, light off, plate ?, wires 1 red 2 yellow 3 blue. Mute's latest gesture sequence was: index-point, victory, open palm, victory, horns, open palm, horns, index-point. The gesture code is still undefined.

The displayed state and wire colours are unchanged, and the gesture sequence cannot safely be interpreted while its code is undefined. I will establish a simple unambiguous code for the next message: index-point means wire 1, victory means wire 2, and open palm means wire 3. Mute should send exactly one of those gestures to identify the required cut; horns and any longer sequence are to be ignored.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="Your gesture code is undefined to us. For the required cut, make exactly one gesture: index-point means wire 1, victory means wire 2, open palm means wire 3. Do not use horns or a sequence. Deaf should report which single gesture you make.")
```

TURN 5
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
PLATE engraved [ꕥ]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Visible state remains display 0, light off, plate ?, wires 1 red 2 yellow 3 blue. I cannot safely interpret Mute's two thumbs-down gestures. Mute, please speak the manual's instructions to Blind.

The bomb remains unchanged, and the two thumbs-down gestures do not identify a wire under the agreed code. I still have no manual instruction, so cutting would be unsafe. I will ask Mute once more for the rule and the exact wire position in plain speech.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="Please speak the manual instructions now, including the exact wire position to cut. I cannot use gestures as instructions, and I will not cut until you state the required action in words.")
```

LIGHT [?]

WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Visible state unchanged: display 0, light off, plate ?, wires 1 red 2 yellow 3 blue. Mute made one thumbs-down gesture.

The bomb is still unchanged. Mute has provided no usable spoken instruction, and a thumbs-down gesture does not identify a wire under the agreed code. I will not cut blindly. I will restate the three-symbol wire code and ask Mute to send exactly one coded gesture; Deaf can then report which gesture was shown.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="Send exactly one gesture for the required wire: index-point means wire 1, victory means wire 2, open palm means wire 3. Do not send thumbs-down or any sequence.")
```

TURN 7
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
PLATE engraved [ꕥ]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Visible state unchanged: display 0, light off, plate ?, wires 1 red 2 yellow 3 blue. Mute again made one thumbs-down gesture; its meaning is unconfirmed.

The bomb remains unchanged. The repeated thumbs-down is not one of the three wire symbols I proposed, so its meaning remains unknown; cutting any wire would still be unjustified. I will ask Mute to use a longer, explicit encoding that Deaf can relay: one, two, or three index-point gestures for wire 1, 2, or 3.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="Thumbs-down is not a wire instruction. Please signal the required wire to Deaf using exactly one, two, or three index-point gestures: one means wire 1, two means wire 2, three means wire 3. Deaf, report the count.")
```

TURN 8
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
PLATE engraved [ꕥ]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Visible state unchanged: display 0, light off, plate ?, wires 1 red 2 yellow 3 blue. Mute made one open-palm gesture; its meaning is unconfirmed.

Mute’s latest gesture is one open palm, which matches the code I explicitly established: open palm means wire 3. The earlier thumbs-down signals were invalid under that code, but this is the first compliant single-wire response. I will cut wire 3.

```text
act(op="cut", position=3)
```
